title: Golden tests use shared Mage.Server/db and can fail before startup
description:
The golden integration harness starts XMage with `cwd=project_root / "Mage.Server"`, so the server uses the repo-local `Mage.Server/db` state instead of an isolated golden-test data directory. On March 14, 2026, `make test-golden` in `/home/gregor/code/mage-bench` spent 45.9s compiling, then 90.1s waiting for server startup before failing all 14 golden scenarios because H2 refused to open an old on-disk database: `The write format 1 is smaller than the supported format 3 [2.4.240/5]`.

Evidence:
- `puppeteer/tests/conftest.py` starts the golden server with `cwd=project_root / "Mage.Server"` and only writes the modified XML config under `tmp/golden-server/`; it does not isolate the server's database or working directory.
- `Mage.Server/src/main/java/mage/server/AuthorizedUserRepository.java`, `UserStatsRepository.java`, and `TableRecordRepository.java` all create `new File("db")`, so the server uses a working-directory-relative `db/`.
- The repo-local `Mage.Server/db` directory in this worktree is 279 MB, so the harness is coupling golden startup to mutable shared state rather than per-run fixtures.
- `tmp/golden-server/server.log` from the failed run shows the H2 format mismatch before the server bound its port.

This is both a reliability bug and a speed issue. A stale or incompatible repo-local DB can make every golden test fail before any scenario runs, and sharing a large mutable DB blocks cleaner startup optimizations such as a dedicated tiny golden-specific DB/cache snapshot.

Suggested fix: make the golden server use an isolated data directory or working directory under `tmp/golden-server/` (or another dedicated test-only path), and only then consider caching a prebuilt minimal DB for the golden card pool.
